_about: ESL level bands per LADDER LENGTH — authored by Sam, 2026-08-24, in session. Attributed DATA, never hard-coded: a curator ruling lives in a file so it can be corrected without a code change (the pattern set by kb/reference/college_identity_rulings.json).
_supersedes: The absolute bands 0-2 / 3-5 / 6-10 that Sam ruled earlier the same day, which in turn superseded the P-4 pinning 1-2 / 3-4 / 5+. Sam revised after seeing the measured ladder-length distribution.
_status: IMPLEMENTED — kb/_esl_ladder_relevel_dryrun.py, Session 189, 2026-08-24. Dry-run only; no apply has been run.
_why: Colleges run ESL ladders of different lengths, so an absolute rung number means different things at different colleges. Measured over 70 colleges with a readable ladder: L=3 20 colleges, L=4 22, L=5 7, L=6 16, L=7 3, L=8 1, L=9 1.

by_level_word._about: Sam, same session: the high-/low- modifiers collapse to their base band.

_note_L4: ⚠️ L=4 is where Sam's ruling DIVERGES from an even split. An even three-way split of 4 rungs puts the extra rung in the LOWER band (1,2 | 3 | 4); Sam put it in the MIDDLE (1 | 2,3 | 4). L=4 is the LARGEST group at 22 colleges, so this is the single highest-impact cell in the table. Do not 'simplify' it back to an even split.
_still_unsolved: ⚠️ Sam, 2026-08-24: 'Still won't help with the colleges that don't use level numbers.' Correct. The ladder sets only reach titles carrying a rung, and the word rule only reaches titles carrying a level word. What is left is the pile with NEITHER — 543 folds classified `default-beginning`, of which 400 carry no level assertion in their catalog description either. That pile needs a different mechanism entirely.
_note_L2: ⚠️ L=2 is Sam's ruling of 2026-08-24, taken AFTER being shown that the 21 colleges reading as 2-rung are large ESL providers (De Anza, Santa Ana, Saddleback, North Orange Continuing Education) — so a 2-rung read is more likely a PARTIAL VIEW of the ladder than a 2-level program. He ruled L1=Intermediate, L2=Advanced: there is NO Beginning band at L=2, because a '1' at these colleges is not the bottom of their ladder. This is a domain judgment about specific institutions, not an extension of the L>=3 pattern — do not 'regularise' it to 1=Beginning.

noncredit_shift._about: A NONCREDIT course sits one band BELOW where its college's ladder rung would put a credit course, because noncredit ESL is generally preparation FOR college ESL. Applied ONLY on the ladder path — a course stating its level in words keeps it.
noncredit_shift._why: Sam, first on NOCE — "1=B and 2=I (because it is NC, it is generally a prep course for college ESL)" — then "Scope it to NC not just NOCE" when it was implemented as a single-institution override.
noncredit_shift._source: credit_status, per COURSE, from kb/coci_minted_memberships.json UNION kb/coci_minted_singletons.json['courses'], joined on control_number. 118,195 control numbers carry it; coverage over the ESL corpus is 100%.
noncredit_shift._a_correction_worth_keeping: ⚠️ An earlier cut of this rule keyed on the spot-check worklist's `credit_type`, which is blank on 24% of members INCLUDING the NOCE courses Sam named — so it failed on his own example, and was propped up with a hand-listed set of wholly-noncredit institutions. Sam: "You should have data for each course as credit or noncredit." He was right; the authoritative per-course field existed in the COCI staging files all along. The institution list is GONE — do not reintroduce it. If this rule ever looks under-covered again, check the join before adding a hand-maintained list.
